message:
Right on, Danielle. unknown's comment does the same thing that T-Netix/Evercom/Securus/CBS do: it presumes that the families of inmates are guilty by association. It assumes that anybody related to an inmate is somehow more likely to (1) commit fraud and (2) be unable to manage their money, and so these prison phone billing companies are somehow justified to engage in their fraudulent and price-gouging practices.

It's economic bigotry, pure and simple. T-Netix/Evercom/Securus/CBS says that anybody related to a prison inmate must be either a criminal or somebody unable to manage their own finances, and so justifies ripping such folks off to pad their own profits. In short, they inhibit families from communicating with one another, interfere with inmates' support structures, and thereby increase the possibility of recidivism, all so Dick Falcone and his friends can pay for their Irving, Texas McMansions.
